title: Credit and Collections Policy for Patient Payment Plans Installments, Delinquency and Default
content:
This policy governs, for plans under the Patient Payment Plans, when installments fall due, when an unpaid installment is recorded as missed, and how a plan moves into and out of delinquency and into default.

### Part 1. Due dates

1.1 Installments fall due monthly on the due day starting at the first due date; installment n is due on the first due date advanced by n minus one calendar months, falling back to the month's last day where the month has no such day.

1.2 A reminder, or with automatic debit a pre-debit notice, goes out the tier's reminder lead time in days before each due date.

### Part 2. Automatic debit

2.1 Automatic debit takes the installment on the due date. A failed debit is retried the tier's retry count of times, the tier's retry interval of days apart. After the tier's number of returned debits, automatic debit is removed.

### Part 3. Missed installments

3.1 An installment is recorded as missed only when it is still unpaid at the end of the tier's grace days after the installment's due date. The due date is the first due date advanced by the installment number minus one calendar months (falling back to the month's last day), the grace days are counted in calendar days starting the day after that due date, and the miss may be recorded only from the day after the last grace day. The first due date is read from the system record of the plan.

3.2 The patient is notified within the tier's miss-notice period in calendar days.

| Day relative to the due date (hypothetical grace of 10 days, due 10 March) | Installment still unpaid | May the miss be recorded? |
|---|---|---|
| 10 March (due date) | Yes | No |
| 11 March to 20 March (grace days 1 to 10) | Yes | No |
| 21 March (day after the last grace day) | Yes | Yes |

### Part 4. Delinquency, cure and default

4.1 The count of missed installments since the plan was last current is the number of installments recorded as missed, from the later of the plan's first due date and its most recent cure or reinstatement up to the handling date, for which no payment of that installment is recorded.

4.2 The plan becomes delinquent when that count reaches the tier's delinquency count.

4.3 Paying every missed installment inside the tier's cure window, counted from the date the plan became delinquent, returns the plan to active.

4.4 The plan defaults when that count reaches the tier's default count, or when the cure window ends uncured. A warning goes out the tier's default-warning lead time in days before the window ends.

4.5 The cure window is counted in calendar days from the day after the date the plan became delinquent, and a default for an uncured window is recorded only from the day after its last day.

| Missed since last current, compared with the tier's counts | Plan state that follows |
|---|---|
| Reaches the delinquency count | Delinquent |
| Reaches the default count | Defaulted |

Cure window boundary (hypothetical 30-day window, delinquent since 1 April): day 1 is 2 April and day 30 is 1 May. A default for an uncured window may be recorded from 2 May; on 1 May it may not.

### Part 5. Overpayment of an installment

5.1 A payment larger than the installment due is applied to that installment and the excess is treated as a prepayment.
